item.content:encoded:
1. Introduction

Welcome to McCourt Photography. We are committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring that your personal information is handled in a safe and responsible manner. This Privacy Policy outlines how we collect, use, and protect your information when you use our website mccourtphotography.co.uk and our services.

2. Information We Collect

We collect information to provide better services to our clients. This information includes:

  • Personal Information: This includes your name, email address, phone number, postal address, and any other details you provide when contacting us or booking our services.
  • Photography Session Details: Information related to your wedding or event, such as date, location, and specific preferences or requests.
  • Images and Videos: Photographs and videos taken during your wedding or event.
  • Payment Information: Payment details when you purchase our services. We use secure payment gateways, and we do not store your credit card information on our servers.
  • Technical Information: We may collect data about your usage of our Website, including IP addresses, browser type, and pages visited. This helps us improve our Website and services.

3. How We Use Your Information

We use the information we collect for various purposes, including:

  • Providing Services: To deliver the photography services you have requested, including scheduling, capturing, editing, and delivering photographs and videos.
  • Communication: To communicate with you regarding your booking, provide customer support, and send updates or promotional offers.
  • Improving Our Services: To analyze trends and preferences, improve our Website, and personalize your experience.
  • Legal Compliance: To comply with legal obligations and resolve any disputes that may arise.

4. Sharing Your Information

We do not sell, trade, or rent your personal information to others. We may share your information in the following circumstances:

  • With Service Providers: We may share your information with trusted third-party service providers who assist us in operating our business, such as payment processors, hosting services, and editing software providers.
  • With Legal Authorities: If required by law or if we believe in good faith that such action is necessary to comply with legal obligations or protect our rights, we may disclose your information to relevant authorities.
  • With Your Consent: We may share your information with others if you give us explicit permission to do so.

5. Your Rights

You have the following rights concerning your personal information:

  • Access: You have the right to request access to the personal information we hold about you.
  • Correction: You can request that we correct any inaccuracies in your personal information.
  • Deletion: You can request that we delete your personal information, subject to certain legal obligations.
  • Objection: You have the right to object to the processing of your data in certain circumstances.

To exercise any of these rights, please contact us at [Your Email Address].

6. Security

We take the security of your personal information seriously and implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect it from unauthorized access, loss, or misuse. However, please note that no method of transmission over the internet or electronic storage is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

7. Retention of Information

We retain your personal information for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes outlined in this Privacy Policy unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law.

8. Cookies

Our Website uses cookies to enhance your experience and improve our services. Cookies are small data files that are placed on your device when you visit our Website. You can choose to disable cookies through your browser settings.

9. Links to Other Websites

Our Website may contain links to other websites. We are not responsible for the privacy practices or content of these third-party websites. We encourage you to read the privacy policies of any linked websites you visit.

10. Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons. We will notify you of any significant changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on our Website with the “Last Updated” date.

item.title: Best Confetti For Wedding Photos
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
Get Permission First!

First of all before you rush out and buy boxes of confetti, make sure your venue is happy for you to do the confetti throw and if they are, do they have any preferences on the type of confetti you'd be using.

Some venues aren't too happy about the cleanup and even if they are happy for you to do it, most will insist on biodegradable confetti only... Which does make a lot of sense!

If your venue doesn't like the idea of confetti, then you could consider an alternative like bubbles etc...

What Confetti Looks Best In Wedding Photos?

Typically the larger and more colorful the confetti is the better. Larger confetti will float around longer and show up more in photos. Although some people prefer the look of smaller confetti, so if you prefer that look, then go for it... You might just need a little more of it though!

Colorful confetti will be more visible and won't get lost in front of a white dress in the photos. But again this is personal preference, some people prefer the look of plain white confetti in their wedding photos.

In terms of confetti type, the 2 you'd typically choose from would be dried leaf confetti or tissue paper confetti. We always carry a few bags of tissue paper confetti with us to weddings, because its affordable and is a little more "floaty", making it a tad easier to work with. Dried leaves can give an amazing, more natural look too though!

You also get different shapes of confetti. Tissue paper confetti is typically round or heart shaped for weddings. Dried leaf can also be cut into shapes, but will typically be a more organic natural shape.

How Much Confetti Do I Need?

Typically you will want at least 1 large handful per guest... is the typical answer you will hear. But how much actually is that?

Typically I'd say around 1l of confetti per 10 guests. This is around 50g of tissue paper confetti with dried leaf being closer to 100 grams. So for 100 guests, you probably want around 500g of tissue paper or 10l.

The real answer though is the more the merrier! The last thing you want is to not have enough and in the grand scheme of things the confetti will be one of the cheapest purchases for your wedding day and will make for a big impact in the photos!

Confetti Cannons?

These are cool and certainly make a scene!. They can get expensive though, so perhaps handing them out to a few guests at the end of the confetti tunnel for a grand finale would be a good idea.

Confetti cannons are something you may need to buy yourself too as your photographer might not be able to provide them due to insurance concerns... they are technically small explosives!

Tips For Your Confetti Throw

  1. Make sure everyone has enough confetti!
  2. Try and look anywhere but the floor. Look at each other, look forward and enjoy the moment!
  3. The confetti won't hurt you! (unless its a cannon to the face), so don't screw up your face.
  4. Don't walk too fast, us photographers need to be backing up as you walk towards us and we want to get as many shots as possible without tripping over ourselves!
  5. Make sure the guests throw the confetti up and over you, not at you. This lets it float down and looks better in the pictures.

When Is The Best Time For The Confetti Photo?

I usually organize the confetti throw for straight after the ceremony... before everyone gets drunk and right before the group shots, because it gives us something fun to do before everyone has to pose for a shot. It also makes for a nice celebration for after your ceremony.

You could however also have a confetti throw during the first dance.

Any Concerns

I did say the more color the better... however, one thing to consider is if it is wet outside, then there is a chance of the confetti staining your dress. So if it's raining outside, then it's probably advisable to do the confetti throw inside instead.

I think it goes without saying that confetti cannons should be aimed above the couple and not into their faces. It's probably advisable to leave the cannons to the adults too (the ones that arent drunk yet!).

Alternatives To Confetti

What if your venue doesn't allow confetti? Or what if you just fancy something a bit different, then there are other options available such as:

  • Bubbles
  • Paper Aeroplanes
  • Fresh leaves
  • Smoke flares
  • Dried Lavender
  • Ribbon Wands

Do I Provide Confetti?

If you have booked me as your wedding photographer (thanks btw!), then yes I can provide confetti. I have a selection of biodegradable tissue paper confetti that I always bring to weddings just in case. But if you have something more specific in mind, then just give me a shout.

I do charge a small fee for this, just to cover my costs. So just let me know how many guests you have and we can sort it out. Feel free to bring your own though.

Why We Love Shooting at Glasgow Botanic Gardens

The Glasgow Botanic Gardens are one of our favorite spots to go to for couples shoots as the blend of lush greenery and architecture make for an amazing backdrop. Plus they have an indoor area, should the rain start falling... and considering its Scotland, we all know that's likely to happen!

item.title: Stair Arms Hotel Wedding Photography
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
The Stair Arms Hotel is particularly special to us, because it's where we got married in 2023. When it comes to planning a wedding in Midlothian, Scotland, there are few places as charming and picturesque as the Stair Arms Hotel in Pathhead. Our wedding day at the Stair Arms Hotel was unforgettable, filled with warmth, laughter, and a sense of history that truly set the scene for the next chapter of our lives.

The Stair Arms Hotel stood out to us for a few reasons. The location of the hotel is out of the way of everything, away from any distractions. With a large garden for socialising and getting group pictures and out back there are hay fields, with a small woodland area that is accessible for doing more intimate couple shots.

We also found the Stair Arms to be very reasonably priced while not really sacrificing anything you'd get from some of the more expensive venues closer to the city centre.

The Story of Stair Arms Hotel

Nestled along the A68 in Pathhead, Midlothian, the Stair Arms Hotel has been welcoming guests for generations. Its charm lies in its traditional Scottish character, from the stone exterior to the warm, welcoming interiors. The building itself dates back to the 19th century and was once a coaching inn, serving travellers journeying between Edinburgh and the Borders.

I remember first visiting the hotel when my fiancé and I were searching for the right wedding venue. We immediately fell in love with its cosy ambience, friendly staff, and the sense that this was more than just a hotel. It was a small piece of Scottish history. From its well kept grounds to the traditional decor inside, every corner tells a story of heritage and hospitality. Indeed, when you arrive, you’re greeted by a sense of tranquillity and timelessness that feels a world away from the city, despite being such a convenient drive from Edinburgh.

Choosing it for our wedding was an easy decision. Not only did it offer everything we needed. Elegant spaces, accommodation for our guests, and first-class dining. But it also allowed us to create a warm, homely vibe that many of the larger, more corporate venues simply couldn’t replicate.

Pricing

The Stair Arms Hotel has different packages, ranging in price from £1650 up to their top tier package for £5000. Making it a very affordable venue that provides immense value for money.

Ceremony Spaces: Indoor and Outdoor Options

One of the benefits the Stair Arms Hotel offers is it's flexibility for indoor and outdoor weddings. Living in Scotland means we can't really be reliant on the weather, so if you want an outdoor wedding, you either have to be very brave.... or have a backup. Thankfully the Stair Arms has you covered... literally!

Indoor Ceremonies

For those who prefer an indoor setting or for couples who may be wary of the weather. There are charming spaces within the hotel where you can hold your ceremony. The interior décor is tastefully done, blending classic Scottish elements with modern comforts. Think wooden beams, rich textures, and an intimate ambience. As a wedding photographer, this is ideal, as the interior lighting is often warm and flattering, perfect for capturing romantic, candid shots of the couple and guests alike.

Outdoor ceremonies

When the Scottish sun makes a glorious appearance, the grounds of the Stair Arms Hotel make for an undeniably romantic outdoor ceremony. The landscaped gardens are well-maintained, with carefully chosen greenery and flowers that bloom throughout the year. If you’re lucky to have a clear day, the natural light is stunning, gentle and diffused. It’s a gift for wedding photography, lending a dreamy softness to the images. Guests can gather to watch you exchange your vows under the open sky, creating a serene and picturesque backdrop.

Reception Spaces and Decor

The Stair Arms can have up to around 80 guests during the day and 120 guests at night. The interior is a mixture of rustic with modern hints and the staff there can work with you to tailor the spaces to your own style.

The Main Reception Room

This spacious area can comfortably host medium to larger sized wedding parties, yet it retains an intimate, cosy feel. Soft lighting, neutral tones, and tasteful furnishings set the stage for a relaxed yet elegant celebration. Many couples choose to incorporate personal touches, such as unique centrepieces, fairy lights, or vintage-inspired table settings and the hotel team is incredibly supportive in helping bring these visions to life.

Dance Floor and Entertainment

After the formalities are done, you’ll likely want to dance the night away. The Stair Arms Hotel provides plenty of space for a lively ceilidh or a DJ set-up. From a photography perspective, the dance floor is an absolute delight to capture: guests of all ages letting loose, laughter echoing through the room, and newlyweds sharing their first dance. With the right lighting, these moments transform into images that feel both intimate and grand, just what you want to look back on in your album.

On Site Accommodation

With many of your guests potentially travelling from afar, especially if you have family or friends travelling from outside Scotland, the convenience of on-site accommodation cannot be overstated. The Stair Arms Hotel offers a range of rooms, each clean and comfortable, providing a welcoming space for guests to rest after a day of celebration. When our own wedding concluded in the wee hours, it was a relief to simply walk upstairs to a cosy room without worrying about taxis or extensive travel. We just spent the whole day there, relaxing, which took the stress out of the day.

From a wedding photographer’s perspective, having everyone nearby is also beneficial for capturing spontaneous moments. Early morning excitement, last-minute wedding prep, or the delightful chaos of bridesmaids and groomsmen trying to get ready on time, these all become part of your visual story, and I love having the opportunity to document these behind-the-scenes memories.

The Food and Drink Experience

If you’re going to host a wedding in Scotland, the menu can often be a defining factor. After all, good food and drink are central to any celebration. The Stair Arms Hotel is known for offering hearty, well-prepared meals that highlight Scottish produce and tradition. The wedding packages typically include options for canapés, multiple courses, and late-night snacks, so you can design a menu that suits your tastes and dietary requirements.

  • Quality Ingredients
    The hotel prides itself on using high-quality, locally sourced ingredients wherever possible. This means your guests are in for a real treat, from the first sip of welcome prosecco to the last bite of sticky toffee pudding (a personal favourite of mine).
  • The Wedding Breakfast
    The wedding breakfast is where you and your guests sit down to share your first meal as newlyweds. Stair Arms Hotel often provides a variety of menu choices, allowing couples to tailor the courses to their preferences. Whether you love the classic Scottish fare of haggis, neeps, and tatties or would prefer a more continental-inspired dish, you’ll find plenty to choose from. The staff are also quite accommodating when it comes to dietary restrictions and will go out of their way to make everyone feel well looked after.
  • Drinks Reception
    Before you settle down for your meal, guests can mingle over drinks in the bar or outdoor patio (weather permitting). This period is golden for capturing candid shots. People are relaxed, excited, and brimming with well-wishes, which makes for some truly heartwarming images that perfectly illustrate the joy of the day.

Photography Opportunities and Scenic Backdrops

Now, let’s talk in more depth about what makes Stair Arms Hotel wedding photography so exceptional. Since the property is set in the idyllic countryside of Midlothian, you’ll find numerous nooks and corners that are brilliant for portraits, group shots, and those quiet newlywed moments.

  1. The Gardens
    The grounds are beautifully landscaped, with flower beds, trees, and well-kept lawns that frame you and your guests in natural beauty. Depending on the season, you might find colourful blooms or autumnal foliage, both of which provide stunning backdrops for photos. If you’re lucky enough to catch a sunset, the warm evening light filtering through the trees is simply magical.
  2. The Hotel’s Exterior
    The stone facade of Stair Arms Hotel has a timeless elegance. It gives a sense of Scottish heritage to photographs, especially if you choose to include elements like a piper or a bagpiper outside. Even subtle details, like the entrance steps or the cosy signage, add character to couple portraits.
  3. Indoor Corners and Lounges
    Don’t forget the interior! Some couples don’t realise just how many photo-worthy spots are hiding indoors. From the lounge areas with comfortable seating to the charming staircases and hallways, these interior spaces can offer shelter from the elements on a rainy day without sacrificing style.
  4. Surrounding Countryside
    Just out the back of the main gardens, joined by a small path is a field with a small accessible forest area. This makes for a great way to get away from the busy wedding areas, to a more secluded area for intimate couple shots. If you don't mind getting your shoes/dress a little dirty, then stepping into the hay field makes for some epic shots too... Definitely pack flat shoes for this if you plan to attempt it though!

Working with the Venue Staff

An often-overlooked factor when choosing a wedding venue is the team behind it. The Stair Arms Hotel has built a reputation for exceptional service, and that makes all the difference on a day as important as your wedding. Our personal experience working with our wedding planner along side all the other staff at the venue, was absolutely flawless from start to finish. They really took the stress out of planning everything.

Practical Tips for Couples

If you’re considering the Stair Arms Hotel in Pathhead, Midlothian, for your own wedding, here are a few tips to make the most of your day:

  1. Plan for Weather Variations:
    Scottish weather can be a rollercoaster, even in the warmer months. Have a solid plan B for an indoor ceremony if you’re hoping for an outdoor “I do,” and factor in a spare pair of shoes if you plan on exploring the grounds for photos.
  2. Take Advantage of Golden Hour:
    If at all possible, carve out ten to fifteen minutes around sunset for some private couple portraits. The light during golden hour can be absolutely breathtaking. Let your photographer whisk you away for a short session, it’s often the highlight in terms of romantic, ethereal pictures.
  3. Personalise the Decor:
    The hotel’s timeless interior provides a lovely blank canvas, so don’t be afraid to infuse your own style into the decor. Whether that means bright florals, rustic accessories, fairy lights, or a minimalist design, the staff are happy to help you achieve the look you want.
  4. Consider Accommodation Needs:
    If you have a large number of guests travelling from outside Midlothian or even abroad, discuss room blocks with the venue early on. You’ll want to make sure everyone who wishes to stay on-site can do so comfortably.
  5. Schedule a Food Tasting:
    Stair Arms Hotel is known for its hearty, flavourful menus. Make sure you schedule a tasting session if your package includes it, this will help you confirm the dishes you love, and you can also explore vegetarian or vegan options if needed.
  6. Ask About Supplier Recommendations:
    If you still need florists, hair and makeup artists, or a DJ, the venue staff can often provide recommendations from their trusted network of local suppliers. This can save you time in the planning process and help ensure smooth coordination on the day.

Closing thoughts

We have had the rare opportunity to be able to try the Stair Arms Hotel out as both a couple getting married there and soon we will be shooting weddings there, with a couple of weddings already planned in. From our experience getting married there, we found it to be an ideal venue for someone wanting a reasonably priced venue that has everything you could need, from friendly staff, to amazing photo opportunities.

item.title: Strathaven Hotel Wedding Photography
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
If you have been daydreaming about a wedding venue that combines rustic Scottish charm, period elegance, and modern convenience, then Strathaven Hotel may well be the place you have been looking for. Tucked away in the small market town of Strathaven, in South Lanarkshire, this Georgian building has welcomed countless couples through its doors over the years, hosting weddings that range from intimate gatherings to larger festivities.

From the moment you arrive, you sense that this is not just another cookie-cutter venue. The approach alone, lined with mature trees and well-kept greenery, sets a tranquil tone for the day ahead. The hotel itself stands confidently with its classic stone exterior and large windows, hinting at both its history and the thoughtful updates it has undergone to remain a favourite among modern couples.

In this guide, I will share what makes this hotel so special. We will explore the venue’s history, the spaces available for ceremonies and receptions, and why Strathaven hotel wedding photography is highly regarded. We will also look at practical tips for you and your guests, such as accommodation options, local attractions, and how to make the most of the hotel’s scenic surroundings. By the end, you should have a well-rounded picture of what to expect and some extra ideas for planning your own celebration here.

A Glimpse Into the Past

Strathaven Hotel has its roots in the 18th century, when the building functioned as a country house. Even today, you can still spot vestiges of its Georgian origins in the high ceilings, the generous windows, and the occasionally ornate detailing in the plasterwork. Over time, it transitioned into a welcoming hotel, complete with cosy interiors and a friendly team who take pride in upholding the property’s heritage.

One of the delights of a Georgian building is the sense of timelessness it carries. You can almost imagine guests arriving by carriage centuries ago, seeking shelter from the Scottish weather. That sense of continuity is one reason so many couples are drawn to Strathaven Hotel. It is not simply about booking a room for a function. It feels like stepping into a living piece of local history, a place that, despite its age, manages to stay relevant and fresh.

The hotel has changed hands a few times and undergone careful renovations, but the owners have endeavoured to safeguard the original features that make it unique. As a result, when you walk through the corridors or pause to admire the decorative fireplaces, you experience an ambience that is both stately and relaxed. It never feels stuffy or too formal, which is exactly what you want on a day as joyous as your wedding.

Why Choose Strathaven Hotel for Your Wedding

1. A Combination of Old and New

In many wedding venues, you might find all the mod cons but none of the historic character, or all the character but none of the modern comforts. Strathaven Hotel manages to strike a happy balance. You have the grandeur of a Georgian building, plus the benefit of modern heating, lighting, and ensuite rooms, making your day both atmospheric and comfortable. It is the best of both worlds, especially if you love the idea of celebrating in a space that has a genuine story behind it.

2. Impressive Yet Welcoming Grounds

The word “hotel” does not quite capture the sense of space you get here. There are lawns, mature trees, and flower beds that provide plenty of outdoor areas for photos, drinks receptions, or simply a peaceful stroll on the day. The grounds, though not enormous, are carefully maintained to ensure a neat but still organic feel. You might spot birds flitting between the branches or find a quiet corner where you can practise your vows one last time before heading inside.

When the weather is in your favour, the outdoor areas are ideal for capturing beautiful images. If you have children in your wedding party, they can run around safely on the grass, and your photographer can catch those spontaneous moments that often turn out to be the most memorable.

3. Rooms That Suit Different Wedding Sizes

No two weddings are the same. Some couples might want to invite their entire extended family, plus every friend they have ever met. Others might prefer an intimate do with just a handful of loved ones. Strathaven Hotel can accommodate both ends of the spectrum and everything in between. There are function rooms that feel snug and cosy for smaller ceremonies, along with larger reception spaces that can manage a medium or bigger crowd without losing that welcoming atmosphere.

Many couples choose to have their ceremony in one of the tastefully decorated indoor areas, followed by a drinks reception in the lounge or outdoors if the sun is shining. The arrangement is flexible, so you can switch things around based on the number of guests you expect. Best of all, the staff here are used to tailoring the spaces to meet your specific needs. It never feels like a production line. You can talk with the hotel’s wedding coordinator about how best to set up chairs, whether you want a sweetheart table or a top table, and if you have any personal decorative touches in mind.

4. Strathaven Hotel Wedding Photography Highlights

One of the top reasons many couples fall in love with this venue is the photography potential. Strathaven Hotel wedding photography offers a blend of architectural elegance and natural beauty. The classic Georgian frontage is a statement piece for outdoor group shots or couple portraits, while the interior design provides a charming backdrop for quieter moments. If the weather turns or if you simply want variety, you can also explore the staircases, lounges, or hallways, each of which has its own aesthetic appeal.

Photographers praise the soft, diffused light that often filters through the large windows, especially in the morning or late afternoon. That gentle illumination is flattering for both group and couple portraits, helping everyone look their best. Unlike some dark or overly ornate venues, Strathaven Hotel feels bright, airy, and inviting, which goes a long way in creating beautiful images.

5. On-Site Accommodation for You and Your Guests

One detail that sometimes gets overlooked in the early planning stages is accommodation. Strathaven Hotel’s on-site rooms allow you and your guests to stay under the same roof without worrying about transport. If your celebrations run late, nobody has to dash away or drive home in the early hours. Instead, everyone can share a final nightcap and then retire to comfortable beds, ready to swap stories over breakfast in the morning.

This arrangement is a huge perk if you have friends or relatives travelling from afar. Not only do they get to attend your wedding, but they can also spend quality time exploring the local area. From a practical perspective, it simplifies logistics, cutting down on potential stress. If you have an early hair and makeup call time, you can pop down the corridor rather than get in a car and brave traffic.

Ceremony and Reception Spaces in Detail

Indoor Ceremonies

The hotel’s interior spaces cater to couples who want a classic, indoor ceremony. Depending on the size of your guest list, you could choose a smaller, more intimate room or a larger function space. Either way, the decor tends to be understated enough that you can incorporate your own colour schemes, floral arrangements, or thematic elements without clashing with the venue’s aesthetic.

The staff will usually set out chairs in rows, leaving a central aisle for your grand entrance. If there is a particular order or arrangement you want, be sure to discuss that in advance so they can have it ready when you arrive. Ambient lighting, such as candles or soft overhead lights, can add warmth and romance to the space, especially for winter weddings. The acoustics are quite good, making it straightforward to hear the officiant and any live musicians or recorded music you have planned.

Outdoor Ceremonies

While no one can predict the weather, the British summer can be surprisingly kind sometimes. If you dream of walking down a grassy aisle or saying your vows under the open sky, speak to the hotel about using their garden space. They can often provide chairs, a small archway, or other features to create a simple but lovely outdoor ceremony area. You can also decorate the space with flowers or ribbons to tie in with your overall theme.

Keep in mind you will want a Plan B in case the rain decides to make an appearance. However, many couples find that even with the unpredictability of Scottish weather, it is worth considering an outdoor ceremony because it adds a fresh, natural dimension to the event. If you are lucky with the sunshine, the photos can turn out truly stunning.

Reception Rooms

After the ceremony, it is time to celebrate with a drinks reception, wedding breakfast, and of course, some dancing. Strathaven Hotel has larger function spaces that can be rearranged to accommodate different seating plans. Tables can be set up in rounds or in a long, banquet style, depending on how you like to dine. The hotel team is usually flexible about your decor choices, so feel free to bring in your centrepieces, place cards, or custom signage.

If you are planning a ceilidh or a lively dance, the hotel can arrange space for a dance floor. They might shift tables around after the meal to create a dedicated area for your first dance and the entertainment to follow. Whether you prefer a DJ, a band, or a more traditional ceilidh, the staff can advise on technical requirements like power points, lighting options, and speaker placement.

Food and Drink Experience

Wedding Breakfast

The catering at Strathaven Hotel generally garners positive feedback, with a focus on fresh, local ingredients. Many couples opt for a traditional Scottish meal, such as roast beef or haggis, neeps, and tatties, but you can usually choose from a broader menu that includes vegetarian and vegan dishes. Starters and desserts can often be mixed and matched, allowing you to design a meal that suits both your personal tastes and any dietary restrictions among your guests.

Service is typically done by friendly staff who understand the flow of a wedding meal, from the moment guests sit down to the emotional speeches that often follow. If you have special requests, like a particular style of dessert or a family recipe you would like incorporated, do not hesitate to ask. The hotel may be happy to tweak the menu, although it is always wise to check how far in advance they need those details.

Drinks Reception

A drinks reception is a wonderful opportunity for guests to mingle and offer their congratulations while you and your new spouse slip away for a few minutes of fresh air or for a couple’s portrait session. The hotel bar often offers a selection of wines, beers, spirits, and soft drinks, and you can typically include a glass of bubbly or a signature cocktail in your package. On warm days, people can wander out to the garden, glass in hand, chatting in the sunshine. On cooler or wetter days, the interior lounge areas provide a cosy spot to gather.

This part of the day is a goldmine for candid photography. People are relaxed, excited, and fully immersed in the celebration. If you have a friend or family member who is particularly skilled at capturing casual group shots, now is a good time for them to roam around. Alternatively, if you have hired a professional photographer, they will likely recognise the opportunity for authentic laughter, hugs, and the occasional silly face.

Evening Buffet

Once the speeches are wrapped up and the formal meal is done, thoughts might turn to dancing and socialising. However, after a couple of hours on the dance floor, guests often appreciate a light snack to keep their energy levels up. The hotel can typically arrange an evening buffet, whether you fancy classic hot rolls (bacon or sausage), finger sandwiches, or a selection of sweet treats.

Having a variety of nibbles available can also keep people from drifting off earlier than you would like, which is especially important if you have put thought into a big send-off or a late-night moment. Be sure to ask about the timing. If the buffet is set out too early, it might disrupt the dancing flow; too late, and people might have already left. Usually, the staff can guide you on the optimal time to serve it based on your schedule.

Exploring Strathaven and the Local Area

Although your wedding day itself might be fully booked with celebrations, it can be nice for you and your guests to know what is on offer around Strathaven before or after the main event. The town has a rich history, dating back many centuries, and you can still see traces of that past in its castle ruins and charming old buildings.

Strathaven Castle

One of the local highlights is Strathaven Castle, which is only a short distance from the hotel. Even though much of it is in ruins, it still makes for an interesting place to explore or to incorporate into your photo shoot if you have time. The castle offers a reminder of the area’s medieval roots and can be particularly atmospheric in the early morning or late afternoon light.

Local Pubs, Cafés, and Shops

Strathaven is not huge, but it does have a friendly, down-to-earth vibe, with a few pubs, cafés, and independent shops. If any of your guests are planning to extend their stay beyond the wedding day, they can have a wander around the town centre and sample local fare. Many couples enjoy this relaxed environment as a chance to unwind before the big day or to keep the party going once the official celebration is over.

Nature and Nearby Attractions

Beyond the immediate town, South Lanarkshire is known for its rolling countryside and scenic walking routes. If you and your guests are fond of the outdoors, you might consider a leisurely stroll in the area the day before or after your wedding. It is a lovely way to clear your head and soak up some fresh air, especially if you have been caught up in months of wedding planning.

Tips for a Smooth Wedding Day at Strathaven Hotel

  1. Book Early if You Can
    Popular wedding dates can fill up quickly, particularly in the milder months. If you have a specific day in mind, aim to secure the venue well in advance. This will also give you more time to plan all the details and coordinate with suppliers.
  2. Take Advantage of Seasonal Changes
    The look of the gardens varies with the seasons. Springtime might bring an abundance of blossoms, while autumn can add warm, earthy tones to your photos. If you are flexible with your wedding date, consider how the seasonal colours might enhance your overall theme.
  3. Coordinate Closely with Suppliers
    Whether it is a florist, photographer, or DJ, the venue team may have a preferred list of suppliers they trust. While you can bring in your own, it can be helpful to chat with those who already know the hotel’s layout and have experience setting up or performing there. This can save time and reduce the risk of any hiccups on the day.
  4. Discuss Dietary Requirements Early
    If your guest list includes people with specific dietary needs, be sure to let the hotel know as soon as possible. They can usually accommodate vegetarians, vegans, and guests with allergies, but it helps everyone if that is clarified well in advance.
  5. Plan Some Downtime
    Wedding days can feel overwhelming. Between the ceremony, the photos, the speeches, and the dancing, you might suddenly realise you have not had a quiet moment to breathe. Try to schedule a little time in your plan for you and your partner to soak up the moment, maybe with a short stroll around the gardens or a quick chat together out of earshot. This often helps couples stay present and truly enjoy the day.
  6. Consider a Rehearsal
    If your wedding party is quite large or if you have a more complex ceremony planned, consider having a short run-through the day before. You can familiarise yourself with where to stand, how to process down the aisle, and any readings that will be included. It does not have to be a big, formal rehearsal, but a quick preview can help settle any nerves and ensure everyone is on the same page.
  7. Look Into Local Activities
    For guests who are travelling from afar, you may want to compile a list of nearby attractions, walks, or cultural sites. This can turn your wedding into a mini-break for them, especially if they decide to stay for a couple of extra days. Strathaven and the surrounding area have a quiet charm, with plenty of opportunities for leisurely exploring.

Making the Most of Strathaven Hotel Wedding Photography

We have mentioned how the venue caters brilliantly to wedding photography, but it is worth diving a little deeper into how you can maximise the visual storytelling of your day.

  • Use the Natural Light
    Mornings and late afternoons often provide a lovely, gentle light that flatters most skin tones and adds a dreamy quality to photos. If possible, coordinate with your photographer so they can capture you and your partner in these windows of softer lighting.
  • Plan a First-Look Session
    Some couples opt for a first-look session before the ceremony. This involves seeing each other in private, away from the crowd, which can be a powerful moment of shared emotion. Strathaven Hotel’s smaller nooks or even a quiet corner of the garden can serve as a perfect spot for this.
  • Take Advantage of Indoors and Outdoors
    Even on a sunny day, consider scheduling a few indoor shots. The lounges and corridors have a classic charm that contrasts nicely with the outdoor greenery. The interplay of these two settings can make your album more varied and interesting.
  • Consider Using the Staircase
    Many Georgian buildings feature impressive staircases, and Strathaven Hotel is no exception. A dramatic photograph of you descending the steps in your wedding attire can be quite striking. If you have a large wedding party, group shots arranged on the stairs or around them can look dynamic and fun.
  • Get Those Candid Moments
    Encouraging your photographer to circulate during the drinks reception, meal, and dancing will help capture those off-the-cuff interactions that give a wedding its warmth. While posed portraits are lovely, it is often the unscripted laughter and heartfelt embraces that resonate most when you look back at your pictures in years to come.

Practicalities and Logistics

Parking and Access

For guests arriving by car, Strathaven Hotel has parking on site, which is convenient for loading and unloading decor, sound equipment, or simply ensuring that your guests do not have to worry about finding a space elsewhere. Be sure to communicate any parking arrangements or costs (if applicable) to your guests in the invitations or your wedding website, so they know exactly what to expect.

Transport for Larger Groups

If you have a sizeable wedding party, you might want to consider arranging group transport, like a minibus or a coach, particularly if you have guests staying in neighbouring towns or cities. This can prevent any stress about late arrivals or directions, allowing everyone to arrive together, and it reduces the number of cars needed.

Accommodation Blocks

Given that the hotel has a limited number of rooms, you will want to enquire about reserving a block if your guest list is large. This helps guarantee that you can keep everyone close by, which is wonderful for maintaining the atmosphere of celebration right up until check-out time the next day.

Weather Considerations

Scottish weather is famously unpredictable, so it is smart to have a flexible mindset. If you dream of an outdoor ceremony, check whether the indoor function rooms can be set up last minute if it starts to rain. The staff are usually prepared for this possibility, but it is worth confirming so you do not have to make frantic decisions on the morning of the wedding.

Sample Wedding Weekend Timeline

It may help to envision a typical schedule for a wedding at Strathaven Hotel, though you can of course adapt this to your personal preferences.

  • Friday
    Afternoon check-in for guests who want to arrive early, perhaps followed by a casual welcome drink in the hotel bar. If needed, a quick rehearsal for the ceremony in the late afternoon. Early night for the bride and groom, or a relaxed dinner with close family.
  • Saturday (Wedding Day)
    • 08:00 – 10:00: Breakfast for overnight guests, hair and makeup for the bridal party. Photographer captures these morning-of preparations.
    • 10:00 – 12:00: Decorations set up, final checks with the wedding coordinator. Guests not involved in the bridal party can explore the town or relax in the hotel.
    • 12:30: Guests gather for the ceremony, taking their seats either indoors or in the garden.
    • 13:00: Ceremony begins, followed by the signing of the register and some family portraits.
    • 14:00: Drinks reception and canapés, possibly outdoors if the weather is good. The couple might sneak away for 15 minutes of portraits.
    • 15:30 – 17:00: Wedding breakfast in the main reception space, followed by speeches if you wish.
    • 17:00 – 19:00: Some downtime for guests to chat and relax, or the couple might go for a short walk around the grounds to capture golden hour photos if the sun is setting.
    • 19:00 – 19:30: Evening guests arrive, music set up for the first dance.
    • 19:30 – 20:00: Cake cutting, followed by the first dance. The dance floor opens for everyone.
    • 21:30: Evening buffet offered, providing some extra fuel for dancing.
    • 23:30 – 00:00: Rounding off the evening with a final song or sparkler send-off if you have arranged one.
    • 00:00 – 01:00: Guests head off to their rooms or to organised transport. The newlyweds can at last catch their breath and reflect on the day.
  • Sunday
    A leisurely breakfast or brunch with close family and friends. Some couples use this time to open cards and gifts, or simply say goodbye to guests who need to travel. If you want to extend the celebrations, you could plan a relaxed pub lunch in Strathaven town.

Reflections and Final Thoughts

Organising a wedding is a major undertaking, and the venue you choose can either simplify or complicate the process. Strathaven Hotel stands out as a place that combines a sense of history with modern amenities, offering a picturesque backdrop that suits a broad range of styles and budgets. Whether you opt for a large celebration or something more low-key, you will likely find the team here happy to adapt to your requirements, sharing tips and insights to ensure things run smoothly.

Strathaven hotel wedding photography is popular because the setting lends itself so naturally to beautiful images. From the Georgian stonework at the front of the building to the lovingly maintained gardens, there are endless spots for those special shots that will fill your wedding album. Indoors, the light-filled function rooms and charming nooks help you capture the excitement of the ceremony, speeches, and evening dance. If you are open to exploring the local area, you could even pop over to Strathaven Castle for a dramatic extra dimension to your portraits.

In the end, your wedding day should be about celebrating the bond you share with your partner and creating a collection of memories that you can look back on with fondness. Choosing Strathaven Hotel can remove a lot of the usual stress, since everything you need is either on-site or within a short distance. The staff, the accommodation, and the range of indoor and outdoor spaces all contribute to an atmosphere where you can focus on what truly matters: exchanging your vows, sharing laughs with loved ones, and savouring those once-in-a-lifetime moments.

If you are weighing up your options for a Scottish wedding venue, Strathaven Hotel is definitely worth considering. It offers that sought-after blend of tradition and modernity, making it a lovely fit for couples who appreciate both classic elegance and practical comforts. Whether you are picturing a summer gathering in the garden, a cosy winter ceremony by a fireplace, or an autumn celebration among colourful leaves, the hotel is adaptable enough to help you realise your vision. With a supportive team on your side, you can approach your wedding day with confidence, knowing that all the key elements—from the menu to the music—are in capable hands.

I hope this guide has given you a clearer idea of what to expect and why so many couples are charmed by the hotel. Each wedding that takes place at Strathaven Hotel tends to have its own unique flavour, shaped by the personalities of the couple and the little details they choose to include. That is the beauty of a venue that encourages personalisation while providing a strong foundation of service and style. If it resonates with you, I encourage you to book a viewing or chat with the events team. Seeing the spaces in person might just confirm that this is where you want to start your married life together, surrounded by the warmth of Scottish hospitality and the gentle whispers of history in every room.

item.title: Kate & Tony's Wedding at Edinburgh City Chambers
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of photographing Kate and Tony's wedding day at the beautiful Edinburgh City Chambers, which is an iconic venue, surrounded by historic charm. The beautiful couple exchanged their vows in a heartfelt ceremony filled with laughter and joy. The Edinburgh City Chambers, is set against the stunning backdrop of Edinburgh's Royal Mile, providing a magical setting, that made for unforgettable photos.

The meal - Scotts Kitchen

After the ceremony, we all took a relaxed stroll through Edinburgh's bustling streets. The entire wedding party walked from the City Chambers, to Scott's Kitchen, which is a cozy and welcoming venue in the heart of Edinburgh.

At Scott's Kitchen, we all enjoyed delicious food and a warm atmosphere. It was a lovely moment of downtime, where everyone got to relax, mingle and unwind after the ceremony.

We had some time after the meal to venture onto the iconic Victoria street for a small couples session, where we got some pictures of the couple against the stunning backdrop that Victoria street has to offer.

The party! - Voodoo Rooms

To wrap up their incredible day, Kate and Tony chose the Voodoo Rooms, an iconic venue known for its stylish interiors and vibrant atmosphere. Here, the celebrations transitioned seamlessly into an energetic evening filled with laughter, dancing, and great music. The Voodoo Rooms provided the ideal backdrop for an unforgettable party, capturing the couple's fun-loving spirit and leaving lasting memories for everyone present. Kate and Tony's Edinburgh wedding was truly a beautiful celebration from start to finish.

Edinburgh City Chambers - A Beautiful Place to Say "I Do"

We love photographing weddings at the Edinburgh City Chambers. It's such a charming and historic venue, right in the heart of Edinburgh. With it being located right off the Royal mile, it's easy to get to with public transport and is a short walk from many historic buildings, such as Edinburgh Castle!.

The architecture at the Edinburgh City Chambers and the surrounding buildings, make for an amazing backdrop in pictures. Edinburgh really leaves you spoiled for choice!

The City Chambers themselves have a warm, intimate feel, despite the grand appearance. Making it perfect for both small and large celebrations. Every room seems to tell its own story, adding an extra layer of character and charm to your wedding photos.

item.title: Dr Bells Baths Wedding Photography
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to wedding venues in Edinburgh, Dr. Bell’s Baths in Leith is one of the most distinctive spaces you’ll come across. It effortlessly merges the building’s fascinating past with a modern, urban edge. From my first visit, I knew this place wasn’t just another cookie-cutter venue—it radiates character and a sense of history that feels both captivating and warm.

The Story of Dr. Bell’s Baths

Originally built in the late 19th century, Dr. Bell’s Baths started life as a public bathhouse for the local community. Over the years, it evolved into a multi-purpose events space, but it has managed to retain the architectural quirks and industrial charm of its former use. Exposed brick walls, high vaulted ceilings, and generous windows that allow natural light to pour in—all of these features come together to create a distinctive atmosphere you simply won’t find in a typical hotel or conference hall.

What truly drew me in was how the venue balances its historic feel with modern amenities. You can walk through the entrance, see the original stonework and iron fittings, and immediately sense the building’s heritage. Then you look around and find stylish lighting, polished concrete floors, and contemporary décor that make it perfect for a chic city wedding. It’s this fusion of old and new that gives Dr. Bell’s Baths its unique character.

Location and Accessibility

Nestled in the heart of Leith, Dr. Bell’s Baths benefits from the vibrant energy of the surrounding area. It’s a stone’s throw from the Shore, one of Edinburgh’s most atmospheric districts, brimming with restaurants, bars, and waterfront walkways. From a guest’s perspective, it’s incredibly convenient—public transport links are excellent, and there are numerous accommodation options nearby, making it easy for friends and family to stay overnight if needed.

For anyone wanting to capture the essence of Edinburgh in their wedding photos, you’re also a short distance from iconic landmarks like the Water of Leith, the Royal Mile, and the dramatic skyline of the Old Town. If you’re feeling adventurous, a quick taxi ride can take you to several scenic spots for those truly epic wedding portraits.

Ceremony Spaces: Indoor Versatility

One of the most appealing aspects of Dr. Bell’s Baths is how it offers flexible layouts for ceremonies of various sizes. Because the venue was originally a bathhouse, you’ll discover vaulted spaces that lend themselves to incredibly atmospheric ceremonies. The high ceilings allow for creative décor options—think fairy lights draped overhead, or large floral installations that accentuate the building’s lofty architecture.

  • Main Hall: This is where most couples choose to exchange their vows. It’s spacious enough to accommodate larger guest lists yet can feel surprisingly intimate if you decorate wisely. Warm lighting can really highlight the exposed brick and arches, giving a romantic glow that’s a dream to photograph.
  • Smaller Rooms and Corners: If you’re planning a more intimate wedding, there are a few cozier nooks and side rooms that can be dressed up to host a smaller gathering. These spaces maintain the same historic charm but on a more personal scale.

Given this is Scotland, indoor options are always a blessing. Even if the weather decides to show its unpredictable side, you won’t have to worry about the day being any less magical.

Reception and Decor

Once the ceremony is over, Dr. Bell’s Baths transitions seamlessly into a lively reception space. The venue’s layout allows for separate areas for dining, dancing, and mingling. Because of its industrial-chic vibe, you can really lean into any number of decor themes:

  • Urban Luxe: Embrace the raw elements by using metallic accents, velvet furnishings, and bold florals to highlight the building’s unique structure.
  • Rustic Romance: Pair the exposed brick with soft draping, candles, and greenery to create a warm, intimate atmosphere.
  • Minimalist Elegance: Let the architecture do the talking. Opt for simple table settings with clean lines and understated floral arrangements.

In my experience, the venue’s staff is incredibly supportive in helping you curate a look that speaks to your personal style. They have great insight into which types of decorations complement the existing features, making the planning process feel a lot smoother.

The Food and Drink Experience

Although Dr. Bell’s Baths doesn’t have an in-house restaurant, they collaborate with a range of trusted catering partners. This essentially gives you the freedom to shape your wedding menu the way you want. Whether you’re dreaming of a modern fine-dining experience or a laid-back buffet that celebrates local produce, there’s a wide variety of options to suit your vision.

  • Cocktail Receptions: The venue’s flexible bar spaces make it easy to offer a fun drinks reception for your guests. If the weather is kind, you might even pop outside for a quick toast under the Edinburgh sky.
  • Formal Dinner or Casual Dining: From a three-course plated dinner to a family-style feast, the culinary offerings can be tailored to you. Be sure to schedule a tasting session in advance if your caterer allows—it’s the best way to finalize the perfect menu.

I’ve noticed that couples often opt for local Scottish touches in their food and drink choices—like a whisky bar or a haggis, neeps, and tatties starter. It adds a cultural flourish that your guests (especially those visiting from outside Scotland) will appreciate.

Photography Opportunities and Scenic Backdrops

As a photographer, Dr. Bell’s Baths excites me to no end. The architecture alone provides a dramatic backdrop, and the venue’s urban surroundings offer even more variety for your wedding album. If you head outside, you can capture shots against Edinburgh’s historic cobbled streets or along the Water of Leith, each adding a different visual flavor to your collection.

  • Indoor Highlights: The main hall’s tall windows let in streams of natural light, which is excellent for daytime ceremonies. Exposed pipes, original tiles, and period details can all be incorporated into unique couple portraits.
  • Outdoor Corners: Depending on the time of year, you might get gorgeous dappled sunlight around the entrance or in the small courtyard spaces. If you’re lucky enough to catch a sunset, Leith’s skyline can be a surprisingly romantic setting for a golden-hour shoot.
  • Nearby Locations: The Shore area is full of striking backdrops—from the waterfront to colorful buildings. If you’re up for a short stroll, you can capture some of the city’s liveliest, most photogenic streets in your wedding pictures.

Working with the Venue Staff

One aspect that’s sometimes overlooked is how important the venue’s team can be in ensuring a smooth wedding day. Dr. Bell’s Baths has a dedicated events staff that knows the space inside and out. They’re great at anticipating logistics, from seating arrangements to working with your chosen suppliers. Having that sort of proactive support is invaluable, particularly when you’re juggling multiple vendors and last-minute details.

Practical Tips for Couples

  1. Book Early: Dr. Bell’s Baths is popular for both weddings and other events, so availability can be limited during peak months. It’s never too early to get your date secured.
  2. Plan for the Weather: Although most of your day will likely be indoors, be prepared for quick weather changes—especially if you’re planning photos around Leith.
  3. Embrace the Quirk: This is not your average venue, so lean into its unique design features. Use the industrial vibe as a foundation for your decor choices.
  4. Coordinate Accommodations: While the venue doesn’t have on-site rooms, Leith boasts plenty of hotels, B&Bs, and rental apartments within walking distance or a short taxi ride away.
  5. Ask About Supplier Recommendations: The venue team often knows local florists, DJs, and caterers who are familiar with the space. Their advice can save you time and ensure a cohesive experience.

Pricing Overview

Pricing at Dr. Bell’s Baths can vary based on your guest count and specific requirements. Many couples choose to hire the venue on a dry-hire basis, bringing in their own suppliers to manage catering and decor. Costs can range widely depending on whether you opt for a weekend date, a midweek celebration, or a more lavish setup.

However, in my experience, couples who’ve hosted their wedding here feel the flexibility and unique setting justify the investment. It’s also worth noting that weekday weddings can offer cost savings if you’re working within a tighter budget.

Closing Thoughts

Dr. Bell’s Baths has a rare blend of historical charm and contemporary style, making it one of the most memorable wedding venues in Edinburgh. If you’re after a setting that reflects the city’s heritage but still feels fresh and modern, it’s hard to beat. From the industrial-chic backdrop to the superb staff and nearby amenities, this venue checks a lot of boxes for couples who want something a little out of the ordinary.

On a personal note, each time I photograph a wedding at Dr. Bell’s Baths, I find new angles and hidden corners that bring a fresh perspective to the couple’s story. There’s a sense of depth here—an intriguing blend of the old and the new—that never feels repetitive. If you’re looking for a space that will wow your guests and let you showcase your individuality, Dr. Bell’s Baths just might be the place where your love story takes center stage.

item.title: Helene & Lewis's Wedding at Edinburgh City Chambers
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of photographing Helene & Lewis's wedding day at the Edinburgh City chambers.

We started off the day getting some group pictures with a short couples session while we waited for their room to be ready.

After the Ceremony, the weather was starting to turn very Scottish, but we braved the drizzle and even attempted a confetti throw in the busy streets of Edinburgh. It turned out to be more of a confetti blasting with the wind, but it certainly got a few laughs!

We then had a quick stroll down Cockburn Street for a few timeless couple shoot pictures. Edinburgh really does have a lot to offer, with some amazing architecture making for a beautiful backdrop.

We were only with the amazing couple for a few short hours. But in that time we managed to shoot hundreds of amazing pictures.

Overall, it was a lovely day, filled with lots of emotion and we am honoured to have been chosen by this lovely couple to capture their big day and give them photographs they can cherish forever.

Below are some of our favorite pictures from the day.

item.title: James & Kayleigh's Nigerian/Scottish Wedding
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
James and Kayleigh celebrated their wedding day at the Westerwood Hotel in Glasgow and what a wedding it was!

The wedding was a Nigerian and Scottish mix, bringing two cultures together in spectacular fashion. The mix of kilts and traditional Nigerian dress was a sight to behold and an absolute treat as a photographer to be able to photograph such a diverse and fun filled wedding!

The couple started the day in their traditional Scottish attire and changed out to their Nigerian dress later in the evening.

This was our largest wedding so far with over 250 attendees and the whole day was action packed, with games from the MC, dancing, lots of confetti, tom foolery with the groomsmen and money spraying... which is a new one to us!

We shot over 6500 photos at the wedding and struggled to cull it down to just over 1300 photos, there was just so much going on!

Testimonial

"If anyone is looking for the perfect wedding photography team- look no further!

Jack and Anna were so professional and accomodating on our wedding and the period leading up to it. On the day, they fulfilled our every request (no matter how difficult and numerous they were).

Leading up to the wedding, we had several meetings to ensure they understood our vision and knew the plan for the day. They were so kind and were completely unobtrusive - we almost didn't even know they were there!

The final photos were outstanding and left us feeling like we made the best decision using McCourt Photography - if I could rate them 100 stars, I would!" - James Ajala

After the ceremony, we headed out to get some group pictures on the golf course out the back of the Westerwood Hotel. We had to wrangle together over 250 people, but everyone had a good time!

We broke out our emergency confetti and lined everyone up for an amazing confetti throw tunnel and we think the pictures from that really turned out amazing.

We also set up some challenges for the groomsmen. We bought a bottle of beer and had them race for it. They were so competitive that they almost wiped out the videographer!, but the photos from that show just how much of a good laugh it was!

The groom also decided he would attempt to run over his groomsmen in the golf buggy, thankfully everyone survived.

After all the antics, we headed back for the reception, Nigerian style buffet and a party. The MC kept everyone entertained throughout the evening with games, comedy and dancing. There was never a dull moment at this wedding.

The couple also switched out to their Nigerian dress, which made for an amazing contrast and amazing wedding photos.

We also got to experience our first money spraying, which is a Nigerian tradition where everyone comes up to the couple and throws money at them to make them happy... It made me wonder why Anna and I didn't do that at out wedding!

item.title: Andy & Eric's Couple Shoot at Pittencrieff Park Dunfermline
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We met up with Andy and Eric for a wander through Pittencrieff Park, known to locals as “the Glen” and it felt more like a relaxed stroll than a photo shoot. We started at the stone gates, letting the long tree-lined avenue pull us into the park, and right away Andy & Eric slipped into their own easy rhythm, joking with each other as we wandered through.

We took a stroll over to Dunfermline Abby, grabbing some beautiful candids along the way. After grabbing a few shots up at the Abby, we took a relaxed stroll back, feeding some squirrels along the way.

We tried our best to keep everything relaxed, instead of feeling like a high tension photoshoot. Andy and Eric were a lovely couple that just settled right into the photos, despite not typically liking getting their photos taken.

item.title: Sabrina & Chris Couple Shoot at Japanese Gardens
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of shooting a mini pre wedding couples session for Sabrina and Chris at the Japanese Gardens in Cowden. This is our first time at the Japanese Gardens and we have to say it made for a lovely backdrop!

Unfortunately the weather wasn't on our side and it was absolutely chucking it down at times!, thankfully though we did come prepared with some umbrellas to keep the lovely couple at least a little bit drier!

Despite the weather, we had a nice wee day out and the images turned out lovely.

item.title: Debbie & Calvin's Wedding at Dundas Castle
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of joining Debbie and Calvin for their wedding at Dundas Castle in Edinburgh. The venue was absolutely stunning, offering countless opportunities for amazing photos.

The castle presented some challenges for us with lighting, but that's nothing we aren't prepared for! We got our flashes and strobes out for all of the indoor shooting except for the ceremony, where we turn them off so we don't pose a distraction. Despite the challenges, Dundas Castle made for the perfect backdrop for what turned out to be an absolutely magical wedding day that we feel privileged to be able to shoot.

We pride ourselves on our party pictures. This is usually the hardest part of the day to capture, because without bringing in flash, you end up with dark grainy photos. Wedding photographers that rely on only natural light, can't get the same level of quality that we achieve in these conditions.

At Debbie and Calvins wedding we had a lovely large white ceiling and white walls in the party tent, allowing us to bounce flash to get lovely soft light, effectively creating a giant soft box. We chose not to overdo it though, because although nice clean light is great from a technical perspective, we would lose the atmosphere from the room. It's a fine balance between getting a clean shot and keeping the feel of the day.

The staff at the venue were absolutely amazing and pulled out the stops to help us and the couple to get the shots we wanted to achieve. Big shout out to Lyndsay the coordinator in particular, who was on the ball constantly to make sure the day ran smoothly.

Debbie and Calvin had both of us for the whole day, from getting ready right through till well into the party at the end of the night, so we could document every moment of their stunning wedding.

Check out our venue review of Dundas Castle

item.title: Lauren & Ryan Wedding at Cramond Kirk
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the privilege of being invited to photograph Lauren and Ryan's wedding day at Cramond Kirk in Edinburgh. It truly was a day full of unforgettable moments and we are so grateful to have been chosen from the couples shortlist of photographers to capture their wedding day.

We started the day off at the ceremony at Cramond Kirk in Edinburgh, which is a charming and historic church, tucked away in one of Edinburgh's most picturesque areas. The church made for a beautiful backdrop to start off the day.

A church does usually give us more restrictions as far as angles, as they tend to be quite strict on where you can and can't be. However, we were allowed up on to the balcony, which made for some stunning photos of Lauren the bride. Because we are a husband and wife team, this meant we could have one of us posted up on the balcony and one of us down on the other side, so we could capture both angles without any disruption.

After the ceremony, we captured the all important group shots, before stealing the couple away for a small couples shoot walking through the gardens. The setting made for some beautiful, intimate moments and some stunning pictures.

The celebrations continued at The Village Hotel in Edinburgh, where the reception brought a modern and vibrant atmosphere to the day. This stylish venue was the ideal contrast to the traditional setting of the kirk, offering plenty of space for dancing, speeches, and laughter late into the evening.

This allowed us to get the strobes and flashes out, to bring some light into the room. We at McCourt Photography pride ourselves on our night time pictures, as this is usually the trickiest part of the day for any wedding photographer. The Village Hotel had large white ceilings, making an ideal area to bounce flash off and create what is effectively a giant soft box. The results are nice soft light that doesn't look like harsh flash photography.

item.title: Aime & Stephen's Couple Shoot at Gullane
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of joining Aime and Stephen with their kids for a couples/family shoot at Gullane beach, just outside Edinburgh. As part of our Deluxe package, they have this included with their package, along with a printed album after their big day. It's an amazing way to break the ice and get to know each other before the wedding.

We met up at the beach and got a few group shots, before letting them loose to play tag and get messy in the sea! We made the most of the amazing weather with sunshine and sand.

In between the chaos, we were able to capture a few more intimate moments of the lovely couple with the sun beating down, making for an amazing hair light.

Lighting can be a tough one when you are on a beach with direct sun beaming down, but we made the most of it and used it to our advantage. On the way back we noticed an opportunity with some tree cover, so stole the couple away for a few moments while the kids cleaned themselves up and we managed to capture some magical and intimate shots there.

We look forward to celebrating their wedding day with them next month at the Hadding Registry office, followed by their reception at the beautiful St Mary's Pleasance. We haven't shot there before, but it looks stunning and we cant wait to see how the wedding photos turn out!

item.title: Dundas Castle Wedding Photography Review
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to finding a fairytale setting for your wedding day, Dundas Castle in Edinburgh is nothing short of magical. As a wedding photographer in Edinburgh, I’ve had the pleasure of working at many venues across Scotland, and Dundas Castle consistently stands out, not just for it's breathtaking setting, but for the truly exceptional experience it offers to couples and their guests.

The Venue and Grounds

Dundas Castle is a 15th century fortress, set within a private estate. It’s one of those places where every direction you look it offers a picture perfect backdrop. Whether you’re planning a classic Scottish celebration or a more contemporary day, the setting adapts beautifully.

The grounds are vast and varied, offering everything from manicured lawns and ancient woodland to a serene loch and rolling countryside views. They also have a large luxury tent available, which they use for the evening reception, which offers a massive space for partying and with the lovely white ceilings, it's great for us wedding photographers too, allowing us to bounce flash and get amazing photos!

Ceremony Spaces and Iconic Features

There are several spaces available for your ceremony, each with its own charm, but the castle's grand staircase is a standout feature. With its sweeping banister and warm stone walls, it makes for an unforgettable entrance and creates a striking setting for your ceremony. From a photographer’s point of view, it’s a dream, both for capturing romantic top-down shots and beautifully framed moments as couples descend the stairs.

Weather permitting, couples can also take advantage of the rooftop. It’s not only a fun adventure during the quieter moments of the day, making your way up the winding stone stairs, but it also provides one of the most iconic photo opportunities in the whole of Scotland, a view stretching over the Firth of Forth, with the Forth Road Bridge in the distance and the Scottish Saltire flying proudly from the flagpole. It’s cinematic, bold, and uniquely Scottish.

A Venue Full of Character

One of the unexpected joys of Dundas Castle is its resident animals! On my most recent visit, the owner’s friendly dogs were roaming the grounds, and there was even a small herd of llamas out in one of the fields. It’s little touches like this that add a sense of personality to the venue, something playful and unique that guests always remember.

Staff and Coordination

The team at Dundas Castle are among the best I’ve encountered in the wedding world. From the first enquiry to the last dance, the staff are attentive, thoughtful, and genuinely invested in making the day run smoothly. Their wedding coordinators, in particular, deserve a shoutout, they are calm, proactive, and have a sixth sense for being in the right place at the right time.

As a photographer, this makes a huge difference. A supportive venue team can help shape the whole flow of the day and ensure that every detail is captured perfectly.

Food and Drink

The food at Dundas Castle is nothing short of incredible. Their catering team delivers beautifully presented dishes that are packed with flavour, not just your standard wedding fare, but something genuinely exciting. On our last visit we tried the prosciutto starter with the beef main course and it was absolutely delicious.

Guests often comment on how good the food is, which speaks volumes considering how often wedding meals blur into one. Here, it’s a highlight in itself.

Photography Opportunities

For a wedding photographer, Dundas Castle is an absolute playground. Whether it's golden hour portraits in the fields, dramatic stairway shots inside the castle, or candid moments on the castle rooftop, the setting offers endless variety without ever needing to leave the grounds.

You’ve got wide open spaces for big family group shots, shaded woodland areas for intimate couple portraits, and architectural features that add drama and elegance to every frame. Even the indoor areas are beautifully lit and thoughtfully styled — perfect for winter weddings or wet weather days.

And of course, if you're lucky enough to get a clear day, the views from the tower with the Forth Bridges in the distance are something truly special.

Some Things to Note

Confetti isn't allowed at the castle, which is a shame, because we do love a good confetti throw, so keep that in mind if you were planning to do this. Bubbles could make a great alternative though.

Also if you want to fly a drone, then you will need permission ahead of time, so make sure to plan ahead and let your photographer know.

Final Thoughts

Dundas Castle is a venue that genuinely has it all. It blends old world grandeur with warm hospitality, luxurious details with wild Scottish charm. Whether you’re planning an elegant black-tie wedding or a relaxed, nature filled celebration, the team here will help bring your vision to life and as a photographer, I can honestly say it’s one of the most photogenic venues I’ve had the pleasure of working at.

If you’re considering Dundas Castle for your big day, you’ll be in very good hands and surrounded by beauty at every turn.
