item.title: Gemma & Gavin's Wedding at Dalmahoy Hotel
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of joining Gemma and Gavin at the Dalmahoy Hotel and Country Club on the outskirts of Edinburgh.

It was a foggy and rainy day, so we had to work around the weather and take advantage of the dry spells during the day, to get outside to do some couples photos and we managed to utilize the front of the building where they had some cover for the group photos. We do love a good challenge and made the most of what the Dalmahoy Hotel had to offer!

A couple of the kids belonging to the guests showed an interest in photography, so Anna was more than happy to recruit them for the day to help get some truly unique shots. Hopefully we weren't breaking too many child labor laws there! Perhaps there is a future in photography for them, because they did an amazing job helping us document the Gemma and Gavin's wedding day.

For the night shots, we got out 2 of our strobe flashes, mounted on stands in opposite corners of the room with a flash on each of our cameras. This helped us bring some light to the dance floor, enabling us to get some crisp photos at night. We like to dial in just enough flash to help us get the shot, without flooding the whole room and losing the ambiance.

It ended up being an amazing day and we truly enjoyed spending the day with Gemma and Gavin, along with their guests. We wish them all the best in their marriage.

item.title: Craig & Rachel's Wedding at Megginch Castle
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of photographing Craig and Rachel's wedding day at Megginch Castle and it turned out to be such a fun day.

We went to a slightly different schedule, getting the group shots done before the ceremony, which was interesting and meant everyone had plenty time to get straight to the drinks table and socialize after the ceremony, which seems like a good idea to us!

This was a religious ceremony, with the brides father marrying the lovely couple. We were told they would prefer no pictures to be taken during the main ceremony, so that was time for us to put the cameras down and become a guest for a while, watching on, fighting the urge to reel off hundreds of pictures of the first kiss.

After the ceremony, we captured lots of candid shots of guests and the couple, mingling along the way. The groomsmen had seen our beer races before and wanted to give it a shot. So we sourced a beer and lined them up. We learned you never come between an Irish man and his beer... the competition was fierce!

Before the sun went down, we stole the couple away for 10 minutes to capture some couples pictures in the woods on the grounds of Megginch Castle and we think those turned out absolutely amazing with such a perfect backdrop, with the trees framing them naturally.

After the couples shoot, it was on to the ceilidh, which was full of energy and great fun to get involved in.

It was a wonderful day to be a wedding photographer and we had lots of fun photographing Craig and Rachel's big day. We wish them all the best in their married life.

item.title: Angela & James's Wedding at Orocco Pier, Edinburgh
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of joining Angela and James for their big day at Orocco Pier, a beautiful venue in South Queensferry, Edinburgh.

The venue offers amazing views of the forth bridges out of the giant glass windows as you are getting married. This presents a challenge for wedding photographers with such a strong backlit situation. However, we tackled this challenge by shooting mostly from the sides and front of the room, making the most of the light coming in and avoiding the need to use flash during the ceremony to balance the lighting. After the ceremony, we were able to get the flashes out and fill in and compensate for the strong back lighting, resulting in some stunning shots.

After the lovely couple were finished their signing, we managed to steal them away for a small couples session, taking them down to the pier to get some stunning shots with the forth bridges in the background.

We were only with Angela & James for a couple of hours, but we enjoyed every moment working with them and wish them a long and happy marriage!

item.title: Aime & Stephen's Wedding in Haddington
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of joining Aime and Stephen to photograph their big day in Haddington.

To start off the day we were with the couple for them getting ready. This is where having a husband and wife wedding photography team makes the difference, because we were able to split up and capture both at the same time. Anna got some amazing photos of Aime getting her hair and makeup done with her family and I managed to capture some touching pictures of Stephen making sure their 3 boys look sharp in their kilts

We then moved on to the Haddington registry office for the main ceremony, where we managed to capture the emotion of the couple as they celebrated their marriage. We then organised the guests to line up outside to do a huge confetti throw at the entrance of the registry office, which resulted in some truly amazing wedding photos. We do love a good confetti throw, which is why we always have a few bags of bio degradable confetti in various colours in our bags.

After the ceremony we stopped off for a quick pint at the local pub on the way to St Mary's Pleasance, which made for the perfect backdrop to grab some group shots with the trees lining the background, then to get in among the trees for some truly beautiful, intimate couples pictures, under the natural framing from the arching trees.

We then moved on to the waterside bistro for some speeches and delicious food and drinks. We had to crack out the flashes and balance them out with some CTO gels to match the lighting in the room and lift up the lighting.

After the food we were on the move again, continuing our tour of Haddington, to go to the Rugby club for party time! The couple had family that were rock band members, who put on an amazing show and really got the energy of the night going.

Weddings like this make us feel blessed to be wedding photographers. We ended up having a blast spending the day with Aime and Stephen with their amazing family. We wish them a long and happy road ahead!

item.title: Orocco Pier Venue Review
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
The Venue and Setting

Orocco Pier sits on the shore line in South Queensferry, with spectacular views over the Forth bridges. It's a modern hotel with a warm atmosphere, perfect for couples looking to get married with an amazing view out the window.

The interior design is contemporary but still cosy, with plenty of natural light spilling through large windows. The views on offer are a dream come true for any wedding photographer in Edinburgh!

Ceremony Spaces

Down the stairs in the main function suite, you have large floor to ceiling glass windows, which frame the Forth Bridges beautifully, making for a stunning backdrop.

The room is large enough for around 100 guests during the day, so is definitely suited more to smaller to medium sized weddings.

Staff and Coordination

The team at Orocco Pier are fantastic to work with. They’re organised without being rigid, which creates a relaxed flow to the day. As a wedding photographer, this is a huge plus and means I can work seamlessly alongside the schedule, while couples and guests feel looked after without being rushed.

They’re also incredibly accommodating with suppliers. From ensuring we’ve got access to the best shooting spots to helping manage timings for golden hour portraits on the pier, their attention to detail really shows.

Food and Drink

Food is one of Orocco Pier’s biggest strengths. The kitchen is known for its modern Scottish cuisine with a fresh, seasonal focus. Every wedding I’ve shot here has had guests raving about the meal, and from a photographer’s perspective, the plates are always beautifully presented.

Canapés on the terrace are a highlight, especially when guests can enjoy them while watching the sun dip behind the bridges. The combination of great food, relaxed conversation, and unbeatable views makes for some of the most candid and joyful photos of the day.

Photography Opportunities

For a wedding photographer, Orocco Pier is a little more unconventional due to the lack of having their own outdoor space to get group pictures. That isn't a huge issue though, because just stepping outside of the hotel and going either to the steps at one side or the pier on the other side, gives you an ideal spot to take guests to where you get an amazing view of the Forth Bridges.

Some Things to Note

Because Orocco Pier sits right on the waterfront, the weather can be a little breezy. I’d always suggest brides and grooms have a plan for hair and veils if we’re heading out onto the pier for photos. That said, the movement can add a beautiful, natural energy to the images.

Parking in South Queensferry can also be limited at busy times, especially in summer, so it’s worth letting guests know to arrive a little earlier to avoid stress. I'd honestly advise planning on not being able to park there at all and getting a taxi, because when it's busy.... It can be near impossible to find a space.

Final Thoughts

Orocco Pier is a venue that combines unbeatable views with warm hospitality and modern style. It’s perfect for couples who want their day to feel relaxed yet sophisticated, and for guests who’ll appreciate the unique setting and vibrant atmosphere.

As a photographer, I never get tired of working here. Every wedding has its own character, shaped by the changing light on the water and the energy of the celebration. If you’re dreaming of a wedding by the sea but don’t want to stray too far from Edinburgh, Orocco Pier is hard to beat.

item.title: Sabrina & Chris's Wedding at the Vu

Overall we had a great time with Sabrina and Chris on their big day and wish them all the best in their marriage.

item.title: Moz & Elliot Wedding at Edinburgh City Chambers
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of joining Moz and Elliot for their wedding day at Edinburgh City Chambers. This was an Indian/British cross over with Moz's family travelling here to celebrate the lovely couples big day.

We were only with the couple for a couple of hours, to capture the ceremony, before they headed off for a party. But we managed to squeeze in around 400 wedding pictures, with a large list of family shots to get. Which is so important when you don't have family all in the one place at the one time very often!

Throughout the 2 hours we did our best to get as many candid moments as possible, ensuring no emotion went un-captured.

We managed to squeeze in a quick couples session before their taxi arrived to take them away from the Edinburgh City Chambers and on to their next venue.

We had a lovely time photographing Moz and Elliot's wedding day and wish them all the best in their marriage.

item.title: Elen & Olivia Elopement at Loch an Eilein
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
Elen and Olivia wanted to elope in the tranquil woods around Loch an Eilein with the only witnesses being us and the Videographer. They asked us if we'd actually be one of their official witnesses for the wedding, which we were so honoured to do!

We started off the day at their B&B nearby for the lovely couple getting ready. We made sure to capture as many details as possible, while we documented the process.

Being 2 girls, they both had beautiful, vibrant pink dresses, which really stood out and made the pictures look amazing.

After capturing an intimate first look, we headed over to the loch, where a range rover was waiting for us to take us to the beautiful spot that they had picked out, next to the water. I may have not been telling the whole truth when I said we were the only witnesses, because there was a family of ducks by the water, who watched on and came up to say hi.

We captured as many candid moments as possible during the ceremony, making sure every emotion was preserved forever, before moving on to the first dance, where the Elen & Olivia had prepared a choreographed dance performance that resulted in some tears being shed from Anna. It was a beautiful moment being out in the woods with a couple of pretty in pink princesses!

After the first dance, we had a stroll through the woods, stopping off along the way to get some stunning couples photos. Elen and Olivia had decided that they wanted to get their feet wet and both of them waded into the water in their dresses, making for some once in a lifetime pictures.

We had an amazing time with Elen and Olivia and their wedding day is definitely the most peaceful and tranquil we have had the pleasure of capturing. We wish them all the best in their marriage.

item.title: Scott & Hannah's Wedding at Dunbar's Close Edinburgh
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the privilege of joining Scott & Hannah on their wedding day, set in the heart of Edinburgh City Centre.

We started off the day with the lovely couple at the Hoxton hotel in the west end of Edinburgh, where they were getting ready. We tried to meld into the background, while capturing fine details and candid shots along the way, while also being on hand to help the couple with anything that crops up.

Once we were ready to get underway, we hopped in a taxi to take us to Dunbar's close, which is just off the Royal Mile, right in the heart of Edinburgh City Centre. As always, we stood in the background capturing as many candid photographs as possible, making sure no emotion was missed.

The ceremony itself was set in the gardens of Dunbar's close, which made for a serene backdrop. There was a slight drizzle of rain, but thankfully we had Anna on hand, who took a break from second shooting and held up the umbrella while the ceremony was underway, so that the couple didn't have to worry about getting soaked!

After the ceremony, we captured the usual group shots and took a walk up towards Edinburgh City chambers to grab a few final shots of Scott & Hannah, before parting for the day.

Overall we had an amazing time working with Scott & Hannah on their wedding day and we wish them all the best in their married life.

item.title: Debby & Bhasky's Wedding at Bowfield Hotel
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the privilege of joining Debby and Bhasky to photograph their big day at the Bowfield Hotel and Spa. It was a Scottish/Indian cross wedding before their even bigger Indian wedding over in India, which we may be in attendance for there too!

They had us both for the full day, so we started off with the getting ready portion of the day. Anna stayed with the girls and I went to spend some time with the lads in their cabin.

We then helped arrange a first look with Debby's dad and then the bridal party, making sure to capture every emotion.

For the ceremony, I was hidden at the front of the room behind Debby and Bhasky to capture everything from a different angle and to get the reactions of the guests, while Anna was at the back of the room, getting some stunning shots from down the isle.

After the ceremony, we had to time our group shots perfectly due to the weather being less than ideal, so we gave everyone some time to grab a drink and then we jumped at the first sign of the rain clearing up to get everyone outside for those all important family photos.

We then went for a wander with the couple, so they could get a little quiet time and do a couple shoot with us. This ended up being so much fun and they naturally fell into the rhythm of it despite saying they were camera shy. We always like to get our couples doing something natural, to ease them into being in front of the camera and Debby & Bhasky were absolute naturals.

We then moved on to capturing the speeches, making sure to get reactions from the guests and the couple. Having both me and Anna there makes this much easier to achieve without missing any moments.

Once it got dark, we thought we would try something new, where we got the umbrellas out and shot a flash up the back to illuminate the couple in the darkness. We think the results are quite striking!

Before we left, the couple said they had brought sparklers, so we went outside again to capture the fun and experimented with some longer exposures to draw some shapes with the sparklers, making for a pretty cool effect!

Debby and Bhasky have said they liked working with us so much, that they are looking at the possibility of flying us out to India to shoot their Indian wedding there!

We wish Debby and Bhasky all the best in their marriage.

item.title: Jennifer & Andrew Wedding at Grange Manor Hotel
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:

We then went for a wee wander with the couple to get some amazing couples photos, which gave them a bit of quiet time to relax, before heading back in to mingle with the guests and get ready for the speeches and food. We try our best to keep our couples shoots as painless as possible, preferring to bring movement into the scenes and avoid awkward posing!

As this was a winter wedding, the night soon rolled in, so we took advantage of this and brought the couple out once more to grab a few quick umbrella shots, which we think turned out amazing. item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had the pleasure of joining Karen and Graham for their wedding day at Carlowrie in Edinburgh.

Carlowrie Castle is a new venue for us, but certainly one we would love to get back to, because it's everything we look for in a venue. From the amazing scenery and highland cows, to the great lighting for the ceremony.

item.title: Edinburgh City Chambers Wedding Photography Review
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
Edinburgh City Chambers is one of the most popular places to get married in Scotland and for good reason. Right on the Royal Mile, it’s perfect for couples planning an intimate city wedding, an elopement, or a relaxed registry office ceremony with iconic Edinburgh scenery right outside the door.

As Edinburgh wedding photographers, we’ve photographed many City Chambers weddings over the years. This guide is here to give you a clear idea of which rooms are available, what your timeline might look like, and how to get the best wedding photos on the day, without any unnecessary fluff.

Why Get Married at Edinburgh City Chambers?

City Chambers is ideal if you want:

  • A central Edinburgh location
  • A short, meaningful ceremony
  • Flexibility around the rest of your day
  • Easy access to Old Town photo locations

It’s especially popular for:

  • Small weddings
  • Elopements
  • Legal ceremonies followed by a meal elsewhere
  • Couples travelling to Scotland to get married

Ceremony Rooms at Edinburgh City Chambers

There are several ceremony rooms available at City Chambers. While we’ll explain all of them here for completeness, the most common room we photograph is the Alexander Suite, followed by The Wee Neuk for very small ceremonies.

The Alexander Suite (Most Popular)

The Alexander Suite is on the ground floor, just off the main entrance, and it’s the most commonly booked room (at least in our experience!).

  • Capacity: up to 36 guests (standing)
  • Ground-floor access (fully accessible)
  • Ceremony room overlooks the quadrangle courtyard
  • Separate waiting lounge for guests
  • Small ante room where the registrar meets the couple before the ceremony

From a photography point of view, this room works really well:

  • Good natural light
  • Enough space to move quietly
  • A relaxed, calm atmosphere

If you’re unsure which room to book, this is usually the safest and most flexible choice.

The European Suite

The European Suite is a more traditional, grand room on the first floor.

  • Capacity: up to 70 guests (standing)
  • Access via main staircase or lift
  • Historic paintings lining the walls
  • Overlooks the quadrangle courtyard

This room has a very regal feel and suits couples wanting a more formal setting. Even if you don’t choose this room, it’s good to know it exists as an option for larger guest numbers.

The Council Chamber

The Council Chamber is the largest ceremony room at City Chambers and sits on the seventh floor.

  • Capacity: up to 110 guests (standing)
  • Views across the Edinburgh skyline
  • Domed ceiling, murals, and a striking fireplace
  • Access via stairs or lift

This room feels very grand and works best for larger weddings. Edinburgh Registration Services encourage couples to personalise ceremonies here, which makes it popular for those wanting something more bespoke.

The Wee Neuk (Smallest Room)

The Wee Neuk is the smallest ceremony room and is perfect for couples who want something very simple.

  • Monday to Thursday only
  • For the couple and two witnesses (we can also be in there)
  • Standard ceremony only

This room is often chosen by couples:

  • Eloping to Edinburgh
  • Having a legal ceremony before a larger celebration abroad
  • Wanting a no-fuss, registration-only ceremony

It’s small, quiet, and very intimate — ideal if the legal part of the day is all you’re after.

A Typical City Chambers Wedding Timeline

One of the biggest questions couples ask is “How much time do we actually need?”

Here’s a realistic example for a City Chambers wedding with photography:

Example 2-Hour Timeline

15–20 minutes before ceremony

  • Guests arrive and wait in the lounge
  • Final paperwork and chats with the registrar
  • A few relaxed pre-ceremony photos if time allows

Ceremony (15–20 minutes)

  • Short, personal, and relaxed
  • Key moments happen quickly, so experience matters here

Immediately after ceremony (10–15 minutes)

  • Congratulations
  • Confetti (where permitted)
  • Quick group photos nearby

Couple portraits (20–30 minutes)

  • Royal Mile
  • Parliament Square
  • Nearby Old Town closes
  • St Giles’ Cathedral area

This leaves you plenty of time to head off to your restaurant, reception, or next location without feeling rushed.

Best Photo Locations Near City Chambers

One of the biggest advantages of getting married here is that you don’t need to travel far at all.

Royal Mile

Perfect for natural, documentary-style photos with a real Edinburgh feel. We typically take a wee walk out there with the couple for a small couples session. If you have a confetti throw in mind, then we can step off the grounds of the Edinburgh City Chambers and do it in the street too.

Old Town Closes

Great for:

  • More intimate portraits
  • Sheltered spots if it rains
  • A slightly more cinematic look

We’ll always adapt locations on the day depending on crowds, weather, and how relaxed you want things to feel.

What If It Rains?

Honestly? It really doesn’t matter. Our kit is rain proof and we always bring umbrellas for the couple.

Edinburgh rain often adds atmosphere, and City Chambers is surrounded by:

  • Covered walkways
  • Sheltered streets
  • Beautiful stone buildings that look great in any weather

Some of our favorite City Chambers wedding photos have been taken on rainy days.

How Much Photography Coverage Do You Need?

Our half day package is typically Ideal for weddings at the Edinburgh City Chambers. This typically has plenty time baked in so you can get your ceremony photos, group photos, couple shoot and then if you have a venue you are going on to after, then we can tag along and get any speeches etc...

Final Thoughts on Getting Married at City Chambers

Edinburgh City Chambers is ideal if you’re looking for:

  • A relaxed, central wedding location
  • An intimate ceremony
  • Iconic Edinburgh backdrops

Edinburgh City Chambers Wedding Photographer

If you’re planning a City Chambers wedding and want natural, relaxed wedding photography that feels like you, we’d love to hear from you.

Get in touch to see if we have your date available.

item.title: A Bride’s Guide to Mastering the Mood in Scotland’s Atmospheric Venues
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
Scotland offers some of the most spectacular venues and settings for an unforgettable wedding. From the moody cityscapes of Edinburgh and Glasgow to the misty hills of Glencoe and the Highlands, they serve as characters for your big day. But they do trigger a big question with brides: what if the photographs come out too dark?

Mastering the mood of a low-light Scottish venue isn’t about flooding it with artificial brightness until it looks like a conference room. It’s about having a photographer with the right tools and instincts to make that darkness work for your special day.

Why a dark venue can be a photographer’s dream

That cinematic, immersive quality you’ve saved to your mood board is totally achievable if your photographer has the experience and gear to handle it. You don’t need to become a camera expert to understand what makes a low-light photographer fantastic, but understanding the ‘why’ behind the lens can help settle those wedding planning nerves.

Mastering a low-light Scottish venue isn’t about flooding it with artificial brightness. The secret lies in high-end,"fast" optics; lenses with a very wide maximum aperture that can gather light far more efficiently than a standard kit lens. Ultimately, this means they can shoot in much darker conditions while still producing incredible images. 

These specialised low aperture lenses (often called prime lenses) are a significant investment, but many of the UK’s top wedding specialists curate at least a proportion of their professional set ups through MPB. By opting for the circular economy, photographers can source a wider range of ‘broken in’, top-tier, reliable equipment, ensuring they always have the most capable tools needed to turn a dark Scottish ceremony into a cinematic memory. 

Discussing early on with your photographer the aesthetic you want to achieve, and the professional kit they have available to capture it in low light, will ensure you can stop worrying about the shadows and start looking forward to the atmosphere. 

Embracing the grain

A less experienced photographer might see noise and graininess in an image as a flaw, but for a pro this presents an organic cinematic quality that can actually be quite beautiful. From the whispered speeches to the first dance, low-light conditions require higher ISO levels. Modern cameras can handle this incredibly well, and a sharp, well-exposed image with a touch of cinematic grain is always better than an underexposed, blurred shot that loses the emotion of the moment.

Being purposeful with flash

In a darker setting, natural light isn’t always a viable option. Your photographer should use flash purposefully. When bounced or diffused against the right backdrop, flash creates a soft, flattering glow rather than the more unflattering and harsh ‘deer in headlights’ look. It’s about adding subtle fill light or dramatic backlighting to enhance the atmosphere you’ve spent months creating. 

3 questions to ask your photographer

Whether you’re still in early conversations with a photographer or narrowing down a shortlist, these three questions will quickly reveal if a photographer is prepared for Scotland’s historic venues and atmospheric interiors.

“How do you handle Blue Hour transitions without losing the atmosphere?”

Blue Hour is the brief window after sunset when the sky softens to a deep, luminous blue. It’s also one of the most creative opportunities a photographer has at their disposal in a Scottish autumn or winter wedding. A professional who plans for it, rather than reacts to it, will already know how to balance the ambient exterior light against interior warmth, without letting either dominate the frame.

“What is your backup plan for a ceremony in a room with no natural light?”

Some of Scotland’s most dramatic ceremony spaces, whether it’s an underground vault in Edinburgh or a candlelit Highland chapel, may offer virtually no natural light. This isn’t a problem with the right specific approach, and you will want to hear a confident answer about their approach to off-camera lighting, high-ISO capability, or reflective flash technique. Hesitation here is a red flag; confidence is a sign they’ve mastered the dark before. 

“Do you use prime lenses or zooms for the reception dance floor?”

While a more technical based question, the answer here will tell you a great deal about the type of photos you’ll get back. Prime lenses have a fixed focal length, with no zoom, and are  widely considered the mood kings of low-light photography. They are faster and sharper in low light, producing that creamy, blurred background that makes a dance floor shot feel like a piece of art rather than a quick snap from a disposable camera.

Scotland’s most beautiful weddings don’t happen in spite of the shadows; they happen because of them. The drama of a candlelit vault or the intimacy of a reception held under the low stone arch of a Highland keep are the reason couples choose these backdrops for their big day. Just be sure to choose a photographer who sees a dark ceiling or a moody sky as a possibility, rather than a problem. Knowing your photographer is backed by the right professional grade kit, means you can trust them to lean into the darkness, allowing you a masterclass in atmosphere.

item.title: Sharon & Aadam Christmas Wedding at Bilbirnie House
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We were so happy to be part of Sharon and Aadam's wedding day at the beautiful Bilbirnie House.

If you haven't been to Bilbirnie House before, it is honestly one of those venues that just works for photography. Great spaces, gorgeous grounds, and a character to the building that gives you something interesting to shoot around every corner.

Sharon and Aadam went all out with their Christmas theme, and the decorations throughout the venue were absolutely beautiful. Honestly, walking in and seeing everything dressed up for Christmas made it feel like something straight out of a festive film set. It added a real warmth and atmosphere to the whole day that came through in every single image.

Winter weddings do come with their challenges when it comes to daylight, but that is honestly part of what makes them so enjoyable to shoot. The low light, the candles, the fairy lights, the festive glow, it all adds up to something a bit different and a lot special.

We turn the darker nights into an opportunity. We get the flashes out and get creative with it.

Sharon and Aadam were a joy to work with, and their guests made the day everything it should be. Big congratulations to the two of them, we loved every minute of being part of it!

item.title: Jo & Angus Wedding at Edinburgh Registry Office
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had such a brilliant day with Jo and Angus for their Edinburgh wedding, and it was one of those days that took us to some really great spots across the city.

We kicked things off at the Edinburgh Registry Office, which is always a lovely setting for a ceremony. There is something really charming about a registry office wedding, it feels relaxed and personal, and it sets a great tone for the rest of the day.

From there we made our way over to Roxy Assembly Rooms for the reception, but not before stopping off at the Rabbit Hole for lunch, which was a great shout and a nice chance for everyone to catch their breath and enjoy some food together before the celebrations really got going.

Roxy Assembly Rooms is a seriously impressive venue. The scale of it is something else, and as photographers it definitely kept us on our toes. Those tall ceilings and the sheer size of the room meant our usual approach of bouncing flash off the ceiling simply wasn't an option, so we switched things up and went with direct flash instead. It is one of those situations where you have to adapt quickly, and honestly it pushed us to get some shots that had a really different feel to them. A bit more punchy, a bit more dramatic, and something a little different from what we would usually produce.

Jo and Angus were fantastic throughout the whole day, and their guests brought exactly the kind of energy that makes a wedding reception so much fun to photograph. A brilliant couple, a brilliant day, and some brilliant Edinburgh locations to tie it all together. Congratulations to the both of you!

item.title: Jenna & Sam Wedding at Sky Bar Edinburgh
item.dc:creator: kriegar
item.content:encoded:
We had such a fantastic day with Jenna and Sam for their wedding at the DoubleTree by Hilton Skybar in Edinburgh. From the very start of the day right through to the dancefloor, it was a celebration full of great moments, lovely people, and plenty of opportunities for us to get creative with our photography.

As Jenna and Sam had booked both of us for full-day coverage, we were able to capture everything from the morning preparations right through to the evening party. Having two photographers always gives us the chance to tell the story of the day from multiple perspectives, and it meant we could document all those little moments happening at the same time as the bigger events.

One thing we definitely had to contend with was the weather. It was an incredibly bright day, which sounds ideal on paper, but photographers will know that harsh midday sunlight can actually be one of the trickiest lighting conditions to work in. Thankfully we were able to use flash throughout much of the day to balance things out and create flattering light where possible. The ceremony itself was the one exception, where we worked with the natural light available and focused on capturing the moments as they unfolded.

One of our favourite moments from the day came thanks to the huge windows at the Skybar. The sunlight created an amazing rainbow diffraction effect that we were able to use for some really unique ring photographs. It was one of those unexpected opportunities that photographers love to find, and at a gay wedding it felt especially fitting to incorporate those beautiful rainbow colours into the images.

After the ceremony we headed outside for a confetti throw before gathering everyone together for group photographs. We then spent some time with Jenna and Sam for their first couple session of the day, making the most of the stunning Edinburgh views surrounding the venue.

Later in the evening, as the sun started to drop lower in the sky, we snuck away for a second mini couple shoot. Golden hour always brings a different atmosphere, and it gave us the chance to create another set of portraits with a completely different feel from those taken earlier in the day.

Throughout the reception we captured plenty of natural candid moments, family photographs, and all the fun that comes with a wedding celebration. We always encourage guests to come and find us if there are family photos they'd like taken, and it's a great way to make sure everyone leaves with memories of the people who matter most to them.

Jenna and Sam were such a sweet couple to work with and made us feel welcome from the moment we arrived. Their friends and family brought so much warmth and energy to the day, and it was an absolute pleasure to be part of their wedding. Congratulations again to you both, we loved every minute of it!

We recieved a lovely review from Jenna and Sam - "5 Stars is not enough for Jack and Anna. They are REMARKABLE! Jack and Anna captured our wedding in April, and they were beyond fantastic. They fit into our wedding day so perfectly that by the end, it felt like they were part of our day as friends with us.
Both are so kind and sweet, even going to lengths that are out of their photography skills to bring little touches to our day, to make our lives that much easier. They are both the most beautiful souls and people and have hearts of gold. From initial inquiry emails, through to pricing, availability and booking, they are so professional, kind and accommodating. We had a pre-wedding photoshoot with them, and we clicked instantly. They are super professional and friendly, making you feel so relaxed, so your pictures are just natural and wonderful. The pictures, they will not disappoint, honestly, they are the most wonderful pictures, THEY ARE SPECTACULAR! We have our entire day pictured from start to finish in a way that makes us laugh and cry and remember the entire day from start to finish. Jack and Anna, thank you, thank you for being THE BEST. I cannot review you or recommend you more highly, just nothing short of Incredible, both on a personal and professional level! Thank you!"
